item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract and is the patch I would merge after a small correction. A expands scope into explicitly prohibited association APIs and global request-body/retry behavior.","reasons":["B adds the exact Upload signature, validates filename/content, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", and produces a replayable *bytes.Reader.","B keeps FilesOption and Add behavior unchanged, while A adds multiple association options and multipart-field machinery despite the explicit prohibition.","A refactors RawClient body ownership, Content-Length, seeking, and retry semantics across the SDK, creating broad compatibility risk outside the requested convenience API.","Neither patch routes Upload through FilesService.Add as required; both duplicate Add's request/response path. This is B's main implementation defect and is straightforward to fix by returning s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...)."],"risks_a":["Explicit contract violations: adds association fields and refactors unrelated request/retry machinery.","Changes caller-body closing semantics and retry behavior globally, so preserving Add's existing behavior is questionable.","Upload bypasses Add and duplicates request construction, decoding, and missing-data handling instead of centralizing them there."],"risks_b":["Upload bypasses Add, duplicating its request/response implementation contrary to the contract.","Tests retry with bytes.NewReader input rather than a genuinely streamed/non-replayable source, so they do not prove buffering fixes the reported streamed-content case.","No visible test verifies propagation of a source-reader failure."]}
